rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اعتراك means that something befell or came upon him; its root image is approaching his place or side.
rows.anchor: أصله من إعتراه بمعنى قصد عراه أي محله وناحيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By evil, they mean madness, accusing Hūd of having lost his reason.
rows.anchor: أرادوا به قاتلهم الله تعالى الجنون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The indefinite evil can minimize their insolence: they attribute it to only some of their gods, not all.
rows.anchor: قيل : للتقليل كأنهم لم يبالغوا في العتو كما ينبيء عنه نسبة ذلك إلى بعض آلهتهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, indefiniteness magnifies the harm, implying that only someone afflicted by much evil would speak so irrationally; naming some gods also magnifies their power.
rows.anchor: وقيل : للتكثير إشارة إلى أن ما قاله لا يصدر إلا عمن أصيب بكثير سوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is empty after a restrictive construction: the underlying sense is that they say nothing except this statement, with omitted general and specific terms.
rows.anchor: والجملة مقول القول وإلا لغو لأن الإستثناء مفرغ وأصله أن نقول قولا إلا قولنا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes اعتراك itself as the excepted item, intended as a quoted word, so no omitted قول is needed.
rows.anchor: هو المستثنى لأنه أريد به لفظه فلا حاجة إلى تقدير قول بعد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The accusation explains why Hūd challenged them after they said they would not heed him.
rows.anchor: قيل : بيان سبب ما صدر عن هود عليه السلام بعد ما ذكروا من عدم إلتفاتهم لقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it reinforces their preceding refusals to abandon their gods or believe Hūd.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو مقرر لما مر من قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their defiance escalates from disputing his proof, to refusing his command, to rejecting his credibility, and finally portraying him as mad.
rows.anchor: سلكوا طريق المخالفة والعناد إلى سبيل الترقي من السيء إلى الأسوأ حيث أخبروا أولا عن عدم مجيئه بالبينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lack of a conjunction may show that this sentence is not merely emphatic like the first two, though it still confirms what preceded.
rows.anchor: الإتيان بهذه الجملة غير مقترنة بالعاطف كالجملتين الأوليين يؤيد كونها ليست مسوقة للتأكيد مثلهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objects of their association are things they designate as partners, although God never made them partners or authorized them.
rows.anchor: أي مما أنتم تجعلونه شريكا وهو سبحانه لم يجعله شريكا ولم ينزل به سلطانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is most naturally relative; من دونه attaches to تشركون, since making it circumstantial adds no useful restriction.
rows.anchor: متعلق بتشركون لا حال من فاعله أي تشركون مجاوزين الله تعالى

rows.speaker: زمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows ما to be either a verbal noun, “your associating gods besides Him,” or a relative, “what you associate as gods besides Him.”
rows.anchor: فقال : أي من إشراككم آلهة من دونه أو مما تشركونه آلهة من دونه

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi offers a different syntactic account, which al-Alusi considers unsound.
rows.anchor: وللطيبي ما يخالف ذلك وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أني بريء is governed jointly by أشهد الله and أشهدوا; unlike verbs may share an object if both can govern it.
rows.anchor: متنازع فيه للفعلين قبله وقد يتنازع المختلفان في التعدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd answers the charge that their gods can harm or benefit: his initial denial of their divinity was implicit in his call to worship God alone, and he now states his disavowal plainly.
rows.anchor: ولما كان ما وقع أولا منه عليه السلام في حقها من كونها بمعزل عن الألوهية إنما وقع في ضمن الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominal declaration beginning with أن asserts his longstanding innocence; calling God as witness reinforces it like an oath.
rows.anchor: صرح عليه السلام بالحق وصدع به حيث أخبر ببراءته القديمة عنها بالجملة الإسمية المصدرة بأن وأكد ذلك بأشهد الله فإنه كالقسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He tells them to hear and witness his disavowal as a taunt, like a man telling an opponent he does not fear to hear his declaration.
rows.anchor: وأمرهم بأن يسمعوا ذلك ويشهدوا به والمقصود منه الإستهانة والإستهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some permit coordinating an imperative with a statement; others may supply وأقول. God's witnessing may likewise be performative, or a genuine summons to witness as evidence; the author prefers the figurative reading.
rows.anchor: وعطف الإنشاء على الإخبار جائز عند بعض ومن لم يجوزه قدر قولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hūd challenges them all to gather with every idol and cooperate in harming him, then forbids them to delay.
rows.anchor: الإجتماع والإحتشاد مع آلهتهم جميعا دون بعض منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If their hint that their gods can harm him is true, they should all join the gods and attack without delay; the فاء derives the challenge from both their claim and his disavowal.
rows.anchor: فالفاء لتفريع الأمر على زعمهم من قدرة آلهتهم على ما قالوا وعلى البراءة كليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address can include both the people and their gods; some understand it as addressed to the people alone.
rows.anchor: والخطاب للقوم وآلهتهم ويفهم من كلام بعض أنه للقوم فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If even a united crowd of powerful people cannot harm him, lifeless idols are all the more powerless; the challenge thus proves their gods cannot harm him.
rows.anchor: فإن الأقوياء الأشداء إذا لم يقدروا مع إجتماعهم واحتشادهم على الضر كان عدم قدرة الجمادات عليه معلوما من باب أولى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: On one reported account, Hūd stood alone among tyrants thirsty for his blood, challenged and belittled them, yet they could do nothing; this was a manifest miracle and showed his trust in God's protection.
rows.anchor: إنه كان عليه السلام مفردا بين جمع عتاة جبابرة عطاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His reliance explains why their combined effort cannot harm him: God owns both him and them, and nothing occurs except by God's will.
rows.anchor: يعني أنكم وإن لم تبقوا في القوس منزعا وبذلتم مضادتي مجهودكم لا تقدرون على شيء مما تريدون بي فإني متوكل على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense is chosen because it better conveys a performative commitment suited to the moment.
rows.anchor: وجيء بلفظ الماضي لأنه أدل على الإنشاء المناسب للمقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every living creature is under God's ownership and power, directed as He wills and unable to resist Him.
rows.anchor: أي إلا هو مالك لها قادر عليها يصرفها كيف يشاء غير مستعصية عليه سبحانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nāṣiya is the front of the head, including the hair growing there.
rows.anchor: والناصية مقدم الرأس وتطلق على الشعر النابت عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking a creature by its forelock is a metaphor or metonym for mastery; Arabs shaved a captive's forelock to mark that he had been seized.
rows.anchor: واستعمال الأخذ بالناصية في القدرة والتسلط مجاز أو كناية

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr says the expression had become a conventional idiom for power over an animal.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أنه صار عرفا في القدرة على الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is a representation: God watches over creatures, judges them with reward or punishment, and protects whoever takes refuge in Him, like a guardian on a road.
rows.anchor: وهو تمثيل واستعارة لأنه تعالى مطلع على أمور العباد مجاز لهم بالثواب والعقاب كاف لمن اعتصم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the assurance to God's watchfulness in 89:14, “Your Lord is ever watchful.”
rows.anchor: إليه تعالى للجزاء وفصل القضاء ولعل الأول أولى

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf notes the progression: reliance removes fear, naming God as Lord of both sides heightens the challenge, and universal control of creatures seals the proof.
rows.anchor: من حسن التعليل وما يعطيه أن من توكل عليه لم يبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God “my Lord” without repeating “your Lord” intimates special care for Hūd, while affirming that God is Lord of all by right.
rows.anchor: كما في الأول نكتة سرية بعد اختصار المعنى عن الحشو فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seemed never to have lived or remained in their homes, as though they had never existed there.
rows.anchor: أي في ديارهم والجملة قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some parse the clause as a circumstantial phrase describing their state after becoming prostrate corpses.
rows.anchor: والجملة قيل : في موضع الحال أي أصبحوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Replacing the pronoun with Thamūd makes the identity of the condemned people explicit.
rows.anchor: وضع موضع المضمر لزيادة البيان

rows.speaker: حفص وحمزة
rows.claim: Ḥafṣ and Ḥamza leave Thamūd diptotic, treating it as the tribe's name.
rows.anchor: ومنعه من الصرف حفص وحمزة نظرا إلى القبيلة

rows.speaker: أكثر السبعة
rows.claim: Most of the Seven reciters declinate Thamūd, regarding it as the people rather than the tribe.
rows.anchor: وصرفه أكثر السبعة نظرا إلى الحي كما قدمنا آنفا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes Thamūd as the primordial ancestor, requiring an understood descendant or offspring; another says its earlier form explains declension even though it denotes the tribe here.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نظرا إلى الأب الأكبر يعني يكون المراد به الأب الأول وهو مصروف وحينئذ يقدر مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly naming their disbelief, though already evident, censures them and explains the prayer for their ruin.
rows.anchor: صرح بكفرهم مع كونه معلوما مما سبق من أحوالهم تقبيحا لحالهم وتعليلا لإستحقاقهم الدعاء عليهم

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī alone reads the name with tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي لا غير بالتنوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Madyan may mean the descendants of Madyan son of Abraham, with the genitive omitted, or serve as the tribe's eponym; the latter is more likely.
rows.anchor: أي أولاد مدين بن إبراهيم عليه السلام فحذف المضاف أو جعل إسما بالغلبة للقبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Madyan is the town built by the eponym, so “people of” is understood; Shuʿayb is their kinsman.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يراد بمدين المدينة التي بناها مدين فسميت به فيقدر حينئذ مضاف أي وإلى أهل مدين أخاهم نسيبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mission statement parallels the earlier mission to Thamūd: God sent Shuʿayb to Madyan.
rows.anchor: أي وأرسلنا إلى مدين شعيبا

words: ٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ مَا لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرُهُۥ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuʿayb begins with an emphatic command to affirm God's oneness, the foundation of the matter.
rows.anchor: أمر بالتوحيد على وجه أكيد ولما كان ملاك الأمر قدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He forbids commercial shortchanging, which violates justice and the proper delivery of others' rights.
rows.anchor: النهي عما اعتادوه من البخس المنافي للعدل المخل بحكمة التعارض وإيصال الحقوق لأصحابها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation is that they give people less of the goods measured or weighed, naming the measure for its contents.
rows.anchor: قيل : أي لا تنقصوا الناس من المكيال والميزان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: More likely, the warning is against reducing the standard size of measures or weights themselves.
rows.anchor: واستظهر أن المراد لا تنقصوا حجم المكيال عن المعهود وكذا الصنجات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parallel passage in al-Aʿrāf uses “measuring” where this verse has “the measure.”
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في الأعراف ( الكيل ) بدل ( المكيال )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their present wealth means they have no need to cheat people.
rows.anchor: أي ملتبسين بثروة واسعة تغنيكم عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their blessings should elicit generosity toward people as gratitude, the greatest form of thanks for blessings.
rows.anchor: أو بنعمة من الله تعالى حقها أن تقابل بغير ما أنتم عليه بأن تتفضلوا على الناس شكرا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further reading warns that their wrongdoing may make them lose their current prosperity.
rows.anchor: أو أراكم بخير وغنى فلا تزيلوه بما تأتونه من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their prosperity is given as the reason for the prohibition on shortchanging.
rows.anchor: وعلى كل حال الجملة في موضع التعليل للنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they persist, punishment will encompass them all; the warning may explain both the command to worship and the ban on fraud.
rows.anchor: وفسر المحيط بما لا يشذ منه أحد منهم

rows.speaker: زمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses “encompassing” as ruinous, citing the phrase about the garden being surrounded by calamity.
rows.anchor: وفسره الزمخشري بالمهلك أخذا من قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: زمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says calling the day encompassing is more forceful: the day contains all events, so its encompassing the punished person entails that the day's punishment has gathered around him.
rows.anchor: وادعى أن يصف اليوم بالإحاطة أبلغ من وصف العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because a day contains all events occurring in it, its encompassing a sufferer implies that every kind of that day's punishment has gathered around him.
rows.anchor: والحاصل أن إحاطة اليوم تدل على إحاطة كل ما فيه من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment encompassing a person may mean only that one kind reaches each person; the day's encompassing implies every kind reaches each person, a more forceful meaning.
rows.anchor: وأما فيما نحن فيه فيدل عل إحاطة أنواع العذاب المشتمل عليها اليوم بكل فرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's rhetorical contrast is illustrated by a poetic image of virtues gathered in a dome placed over Ibn al-Ḥashraj; the poet is not named.
rows.anchor: إن المروءة والسماحة والندى في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: A scholar explains that the day is the time of all events, so encompassing its victim gathers every punishment of that day around him.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين في بيان الأبلغية : إن اليوم زمان لجميع الحوادث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: محيط may modify عذاب by proximity; another parse makes it modify يوم with an understood “its punishment,” which al-Alusi rejects.
rows.anchor: ( محيط ) نعتا لعذاب وجر للجوار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The threatened day can mean either the Day of Resurrection or worldly annihilation.
rows.anchor: وأيا ما كان فالمراد عذاب يوم القيامة أو عذاب الإستئصال في الدنيا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets “good” as low prices and the punishment as high prices.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن جرير وأبو الشيخ عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه فسر الخير برخص السعر والعذاب بغلائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They answer Shuʿayb's call to worship God alone, which entails rejecting idols, by denying that revelation commands him and insinuating delusion or madness.
rows.anchor: أجابوا بذلك أمره عليه السلام إياهم بعبادة الله تعالى وحده المتضمن لنهيهم عن عبادة الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mocking question treats his prayer as a product of delusion and asks whether it can make them abandon the idols their ancestors worshiped for generations.
rows.anchor: وقالوا بطريق الإستهزاء : ( أصلاتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They portray Shuʿayb as commanded because he taught that his message came from revelation and was entrusted to him for delivery.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعلوه عليه السلام مأمورا مع أن الصادر عنه إنما هو الأمر بعبادة الله تعالى وغير ذلك من الشرائع لأنه عليه السلام لم يكن يأمرهم من تلقاء نفسه

rows.speaker: الأحنف
rows.claim: Al-Aḥnaf reports that Shuʿayb prayed more than the other prophets; his people winked and laughed when they saw him praying.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن عساكر عن الأحنف أنه عليه السلام كان أكثر الأنبياء صلاة وكانوا إذا رأوه يصلي يتغامزون ويتضاحكون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the mockery by saying Shuʿayb used to tell them that prayer enjoins right and forbids indecency.
rows.anchor: إن الصلاة تأمر بالمعروف وتنهى عن الفحشاء والمنكر وروي هذا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi favors the explanation that Shuʿayb's conspicuous prayer made it a target of their mockery.
rows.anchor: وإلى الأول ذهب غير واحد وهذا الإسناد حقيقي لا مجازي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attribution of commanding to prayer is literal in their wording, although they intend it mockingly; the imperfect verb implies an ongoing command.
rows.anchor: وهذا الإسناد حقيقي لا مجازي غاية ما في الباب أنهم قصدوا الحقيقة تهكما واختيار المضارع ليدل على العموم بحسب الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One parse supplies تكليف before أن and treats the preposition as omitted, a regular construction; another says a person cannot be charged with another's act because it is beyond his power.
rows.anchor: على تقدير بتكليف أن نترك فحذف المضاف وهو تكليف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative without ellipsis has them mock Shuʿayb for supposedly ordering what lies outside his power or responsibility, but al-Alusi objects that the context gives no reason for such an order.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن الداعي إليه أن الشخص لا يكلف بفعل غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also answer his order to fulfill people's rights and stop shortchanging; أو coordinates with ما and means “and,” covering whatever they choose to do with their wealth.
rows.anchor: أجابوا به أمره عليه السلام بإيفاء الحقوق ونهيه عن البخس والنقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Coordinating the second clause with أن نترك would imply that Shuʿayb commanded their fraud, although he forbids it, so that parse is impossible.
rows.anchor: لاستحالة المعنى إذ يصير حينئذ تأمرك بفعلنا في أموالنا

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muḥammad b. Kaʿb reports that they clipped dirhams and dinars and passed them off with sound coins to deceive buyers.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كانوا يقرضون الدراهم والدنانير ويجرونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some include that coin fraud in corruption on earth and thus in the verse's general wording.
rows.anchor: وأدخل بعضهم ذلك الفعل في العثي في الأرض فيكون النهي عنه

rows.speaker: أكثر السبعة
rows.claim: Most of the Seven reciters read صلواتك in the plural; al-Alusi says the plural and singular readings are readily reconciled.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أكثر السبعة أصلواتك بالجمع وأمر الجمع بين القرائتين سهل

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن قيس وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي
rows.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. Qays, Ibn Abī ʿAbla, and Zayd b. ʿAlī read both verbs in the second person, making the second clause depend on تأمرك: does your prayer command you to do as you wish with our wealth?
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن قيس وابن أبي عبلة وزيد بن علي بالتاء في الفعلين على الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent meaning of “what you wish” in the second-person reading is that Shuʿayb would require them to fulfill the measure and weight.
rows.anchor: أي من إيفاء المكيال والميزان كما هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Another view takes it as almsgiving; Shuʿayb called them to give zakat, according to Sufyān al-Thawrī.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من الزكاة فقد كان عليه السلام يأمرهم بها كما روي عن سفيان الثوري

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says every prophet was charged with prayer and almsgiving, but al-Alusi says this report does not establish the point here.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن أنه قال : لم يبعث الله تعالى نبيا إلا فرض عليه الصلاة والزكاة

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash interprets صلاة here as recitation.
rows.anchor: ابن المنذر وغيره عن الأعمش تفسيرها بالقراءة

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other interpreters explain صلاة as supplication, its lexical sense.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن غيره تفسيرها بالدعاء الذي هو المعنى اللغوي لها

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم
rows.claim: Abū Muslim takes صلاة to mean religion, one of its most important aspects.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي مسلم تفسيرها بالدين لأنها من أجل أموره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if صلاة means ritual prayer, the verse proves only that Shuʿayb prayed, not that his community was required to do so; it may have been his special practice.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون ذلك من خصوصياته عليه السلام

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن وطلحة
rows.claim: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān and Ṭalḥa read the first verb with ن and the second with ت, coordinating the second clause with the object of تأمرك.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عبدالرحمن وطلحة بالنون في الأول والتاء في الثاني والعطف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والمبرد
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Qatāda, and al-Mubarrad take “forbearing, prudent” as sarcastic irony meaning the opposites.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بهما ضد معناهما وهذا هو المروي عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما وإليه ذهب قتادة والمبرد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, they call him forbearing and prudent according to their own claim, and use those traits to question why he would demand such change.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكونوا وصفوه بذلك بناءا على الزعم والجملة تعليل لما سبق من استبعاد ما ذكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ironic reading best fits the preceding mockery; another preference for the literal reading compares their words with the people of Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: ورجح الأول بأنه الأنسب بما قبله لأنه تهكم أيضا ورجح الأخير بأنه يكون الكلام عليه نظير ما مر في قصة صالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The literal comparison recalls the people of Ṣāliḥ telling him that they had previously placed their hopes in him, before Shuʿayb responds in the next verse.
rows.anchor: وتعقيبه بمثل ما عقب به ذلك حسبما تضمنه

words: أَرَءَيْتُمْ إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: The clear proof and good provision in Shuʿayb's reply mean prophethood and wisdom, ultimate signs of perfection and gifts for everlasting life.
rows.anchor: وذكر قدس سره أن المراد بالبينة والرزق الحسن النبوة والحكمة وأن التعبير عنهما بذلك للتنبيه على أنهما مع كونهما بينة رزق حسن

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Ṭībī reads the reply as conceding that Shuʿayb has long been their guide, then asking whether a true prophet and counselor should stop commanding them to abandon idols and sins.
rows.anchor: من كلامه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم كذا قرره العلامة الطيبي

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islam supplies an omitted conditional answer asking whether they would still say such things if Shuʿayb truly had proof, prophethood, and wisdom from God.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف يدله عليه فحوى الكلام أي أتقولون

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī interprets the good provision as lawful wealth granted by God without strenuous effort.
rows.anchor: وفسر القاضي الرزق الحسن بما آتاه الله تعالى من المال الحلال ومعنى كون ذلك منه تعالى أنه من عنده سبحانه وبإعانته بلا كد في تحصيله

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī takes the conditional answer to ask whether, after God's spiritual and material gifts, Shuʿayb could betray revelation or disobey God's commands; it answers their charge that he changed ancestral practice.
rows.anchor: وقدر جواب الشرط فهل يسع مع هذا الإنعام الجامع للسعادة الروحانية والجسمانية أن أخون في وحيه

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some commentators estimate the conditional answer as al-Ṭībī does.
rows.anchor: وقدر بعضهم ما قدره العلامة الطيبي

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم وعطاء
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the proposed conditional readings fit only if the mockers meant religion by صلاة, as Abū Muslim and ʿAṭāʾ reportedly do.
rows.anchor: إن حمل كلامهم على الحقيقة وأريد بالصلاة الدين حسبما نقل عن أبي مسلم وعطاء

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: On that reading, the good provision would be lawful earnings, as reported from al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
rows.anchor: ويكون المراد بالرزق الحسن على ذلك ما آتاه الله تعالى من الحلال فقط كما روي عن الضحاك

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islam argues that if Shuʿayb was God's prophet and had lawful wealth enough to need no one, he could neither disobey God nor comply with the people's misconduct.
rows.anchor: أخبروني إن كنت نبيا من عند الله تعالى ورزقني مالا حلالا أستغني به عن العالمين أيصح أن أخالف أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers lawful earnings free from shortchanging and fraud as the good provision meant here.
rows.anchor: المناسب للمقام حمل الرزق الحسن على ما آتاه الله تعالى من الحلال الخالي عن التطفيف والبخس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the claim that the conditional answer requires treating the mockers' words literally or taking صلاة to mean religion; the answer works with their taunt and the ordinary sense of prayer.
rows.anchor: ليس في الكلام ما يأبى عنه ولا يتوقف على حمل الكلام على الحقيقة والصلاة على الدين

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their real aim was to stop Shuʿayb's preaching so they could keep worshiping idols and shortchanging; he answers that aim by asking whether a true prophet with lawful, sufficient provision should disobey revelation to satisfy them.
rows.anchor: لم يكن لهم مقصود إلا ترك الدعوة وتركهم وما يفعلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not explicitly answer the slur of madness because it is obviously unworthy of reply; instead, he cuts off their hope of silencing him and hints that their own demand is irrational.
rows.anchor: ولم يتعرض عليه السلام صريحا لرد قولهم المتضمن لرميه وحاشاه بالوسوسة والجنون والسفه والغواية إيذانا بأن ذلك مما لا يستحق جوابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning provision alongside proof shows that Shuʿayb has both the reason to preach and freedom from the supposed worldly motive that might restrain him.
rows.anchor: وكأن التعرض لذكر الرزق مع الكون على بينة للإشارة إلى وجود المقتضى وارتفاع ما يظن مانعا
